<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="ניסן_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918081_theRebbe_229" batchId="meluket-_D7_A0_D7_99_D7_A1_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918081_theRebbe_229__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Opening header and date of the maamar for Acharon Shel Pesach 5749.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B"S.</t>
    <t s="1">Acharon Shel Pesach 5749*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The future redemption will include both the drying of the Sea of Egypt and the striking of the River, with the splitting of the river being the greater novelty.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"And Hashem will utterly destroy the tongue of the Sea of Egypt, and will wave His hand over the River with His mighty wind..."1</t>
    <t s="1">And the Admo"r Maharash explains this</t>
    <t s="2">(initially, going over)</t>
    <t s="3">at length in the continuation of "Vehacharam",</t>
    <t s="4">that in addition to that in the future there will be "Vehacharam etc. the tongue of the Sea of Egypt" analogous to the Splitting of the Red Sea which was at the Exodus from Egypt,</t>
    <t s="5">there will also be "and He will wave His hand over the River etc.",</t>
    <t s="6">for the splitting of the river is on a higher level than the splitting of the sea,</t>
    <t s="7">as explained there at length2.</t>
    <t s="8">And the main innovation of the future is that then there will be the splitting of the river.</t>
    <t s="9">And as it is written3</t>
    <t s="10">"He turned the sea into dry land; they will cross the river on foot",</t>
    <t s="11">"He turned the sea into dry land" is in the past tense, referring to the Splitting of the Red Sea which was in the redemption of the Exodus from Egypt,</t>
    <t s="12">"they will cross the river on foot" is in the future tense, referring to the splitting of the river that will be in the future redemption4,</t>
    <t s="13">and "they will cross the river on foot" — this is the main innovation that will be in the future redemption.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The connection between the Splitting of the Red Sea and the future redemption is immediate, and every Jew has the power to go directly from the former to the latter, as emphasized in the haftorah of Acharon Shel Pesach.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B)</t>
    <t s="1">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="2">that this — that "Vehacharam etc. the Sea of Egypt" leads to this, and immediately "and He will wave His hand over the River etc." — indicates that from the Splitting of the Red Sea and its concept, which were in the redemption of the Exodus from Egypt, one can come immediately</t>
    <t s="3">(without any interruption)</t>
    <t s="4">to "and He will wave His hand over the River etc." which will be in the future.</t>
    <t s="5">And particularly on Acharon Shel Pesach,</t>
    <t s="6">on which we recite the haftorah concerning the future redemption,</t>
    <t s="7">and we eat the Meal of Mashiach,</t>
    <t s="8">and this comes in continuation of the Seventh Day of Pesach5,</t>
    <t s="9">the Splitting of the Red Sea,</t>
    <t s="10">through which the connection of the Splitting of the Red Sea with the revelation of the future redemption is made even greater.</t>
    <t s="11">And since this proximity is part of the Torah which is an inheritance for every single Jew, as it is written6</t>
    <t s="12">"Torah was commanded to us by Moshe, an inheritance for the congregation of Yaakov",</t>
    <t s="13">there exists the power for every single Jew,</t>
    <t s="14">men, women, and children,</t>
    <t s="15">to come from the Splitting of the Red Sea,</t>
    <t s="16">immediately and instantly, to the future redemption,</t>
    <t s="17">without any delay even for the blink of an eye7.</t>
    <t s="18">And this — that it is within the power of every single Jew to come immediately to the revelation of the future redemption — is also emphasized in what is written</t>
    <t s="19">(in the haftorah of Acharon Shel Pesach)</t>
    <t s="20">"And the spirit of Hashem shall rest upon him..."8,</t>
    <t s="21">for "him" refers to Mashiach</t>
    <t s="22">("And a shoot shall emerge from the stem of Yishai..."9),</t>
    <t s="23">and nevertheless they instituted that every Jew should say on Yom Tov</t>
    <t s="24">(in the prayer recited at the opening of the Ark)</t>
    <t s="25">"and may the verse that is written be fulfilled in us: 'And the spirit of Hashem shall rest upon him' etc.",</t>
    <t s="26">meaning that in each individual Jew</t>
    <t s="27">(as an individual)</t>
    <t s="28">there will be this revelation, and in the manner of "and the spirit of Hashem shall rest upon him etc." with all the details of these verses,</t>
    <t s="29">including also "and He will wave His hand over the River etc.".</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
